problem: End-to-end RL navigation policies with standard RNNs (LSTM, GRU, S4, Mamba) capture temporal dependencies but fail to spatially register and memorize egocentric observations taken from changing viewpoints. Prior work therefore falls back on explicit mapping pipelines (which add delay and rely on a fixed context window) or on stacked history frames.
motivation: Mapless long-horizon navigation, such as escaping dead ends, needs implicit spatial mapping in the recurrent memory. Explicit mapping is slow on agile legged-wheel platforms and its fixed context window limits long range. A synthetic spatial-temporal memorization task shows RNNs recall landmark labels perfectly but not transformed landmark coordinates.
key_idea: Add a multiplicative (star-operation) spatial-transform gate s_t = W_x x_t + b to the LSTM/GRU candidate state so the recurrent unit implicitly learns ego-motion-based spatial registration, then combine it with spatial attention and DML/TC-dropout regularization for end-to-end RL.
insight: The recurrent unit's spatial memory is a bottleneck: SRU alone raises overall SR from 63.5 (LSTM) to 76.5, and the refined gate reaches 78.9. Optimization matters as much as architecture: DML lifts SRU-Ours from 65.7 to 78.9 but LSTM only from 61.8 to 63.5, because spatial memory learns more slowly than temporal memory and the policy otherwise overfits to temporal shortcuts. Attention compression before the memory also matters (no attention 50.5, GoT 68.4, ours 78.9), and swapping GTRL's stacked frames for SRU memory raises SR from 38.2 to 66.3.
method: SRU (SRU-LSTM/GRU): adds s_t = W_xs x_t + b_s and multiplies it element-wise into the candidate state, g_t = tanh(s_t ⊙ (W_xg x_t + W_hg h_{t-1} + b_g)), so the unit can learn implicit spatial transformations.
SRU-Ours: SRU-LSTM plus a refined gating mechanism, r_t = i_t(1-(1-f_t)^2) + (1-i_t)f_t^2, that avoids gate saturation during recurrent training.

Spatial-attention architecture: a pretrained RegNet+FPN depth encoder feeds self-attention over the visual tokens, then cross-attention with the proprioceptive state and goal as queries compresses the map into a 1D feature, which goes to the SRU and an MLP head that outputs velocity commands.

Sparse time-based reward: goal-proximity reward 1/(1+||p/σ||) given only in the last T_r seconds or at random checks with probability δ, plus action-smoothness and safety penalties; trained with asymmetric actor-critic PPO (critic gets a 360° height scan) in IsaacLab.
Training regularization: deep mutual learning (two policies with a KL loss between them) and temporally consistent dropout (same mask across time in rollout and training).

Sim-to-real: the depth encoder is pretrained as a VAE on TartanAir with a parallelized stereo depth noise model (edge, filling, rounding noise), which is also applied during RL; deployment is zero-shot.
Spatial-temporal probe task: synthetic landmark task that separately measures temporal label recall and spatial coordinate re-registration, used to diagnose LSTM, GRU, S4 and Mamba.

setting.backbone: Attention-based recurrent policy (RegNet+FPN depth encoder, self/cross-attention, SRU-LSTM, MLP head), trained from scratch with PPO; encoder pretrained with a VAE
setting.training_data: RL in IsaacLab procedurally generated environments (maze, pillars, stairs, pits; start-goal up to 30 m); encoder pretrained on TartanAir synthetic depth with noise augmentation
setting.observation: single front-facing stereo depth image (105°x78° FoV, 10 m range) plus proprioception (linear/angular velocity, projected gravity, previous action) and relative goal position from state estimation
setting.action_space: continuous linear and angular velocity commands at 5 Hz, passed to a learned 50 Hz locomotion controller
setting.privileged: Critic only (training): 360° height scan and noise-free observations. At test time the policy uses LiDAR-inertial state estimation for velocity, gravity and relative goal position, but no map.

numbers_note: No standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmarks are used. All results are on the authors' own IsaacLab environments, and the real-world experiments are qualitative trajectories with no numbers.
results: SRU-Ours gets 78.9% overall SR versus 63.5% for LSTM and 61.0% for GRU (+23.5% relative over LSTM), with stairs more than doubling. On ANYmal it reaches 78.3% versus 60.4% for the explicit-mapping EMHP baseline (+29.6%) and 38.2% for GTRL (+105.0%). It holds over 70% SR up to 120 m travel, while EMHP degrades beyond 40 m, and it transfers zero-shot to a Unitree B2W in office, hall, terrace and forest.
limitations: Recurrent memory still decays exponentially, so it is limited to local mapless navigation and would need a global map for kilometre-scale navigation.
It is unclear what information the SRU memory retains; the SRU design is heuristic rather than principled or proven optimal.
Real-world evaluation is qualitative, and the policy depends on LiDAR-based localization for the goal position and proprioception.
